Hi Sophie — thanks for sending the sample. Marcus looped me in for the technical eval. Summary of our initial findings and recommended experiments: 

What we ran (quick pass):
- Models tested: redwood-emb-768, redwood-emb-2048, redwood-emb-768-quant (8-bit-like).
- Eval set: 10k products + 400 labeled queries you provided.

Key numbers (high level):
- redwood-emb-2048: Recall@10 = 0.87, MRR = 0.62, avg cosine(sim) between true pairs = 0.78.
- redwood-emb-768: Recall@10 = 0.81, MRR = 0.57, avg cosine = 0.73.
- redwood-emb-768-quant: Recall@10 = 0.79, MRR = 0.54, storage ~40% smaller vs 768 float.

Storage/latency estimates (approx):
- 768 float vectors: ~120k * 768 * 4 bytes ~ 360MB raw (plus index factor).
- 2048 float vectors: ~960MB raw. With PQ/HNSW and compression expect ~2–3x index overhead.

Observations / risks:
- 2048 gives clear quality uplift for long-form descriptions and multilingual cases, but adds index cost and slightly higher retrieval time.
- Quantized 768 is a good cost/quality trade for bounded infra budgets; still worthwhile to test in-prod for cold-start traffic.
- Drift: cosine distribution shifted measurable between January vs current sample; need running drift detection + scheduled re-embeddings for seasonal catalog updates.

Next recommended experiments:
1) Full offline run across the 120k catalog (we can quote compute and ETA after you confirm).
2) Build time-series drift checks (PCA on embeddings + population statistics + cosine histogram).
3) Define monitoring: weekly drift alert if median cosine to canonical vectors drops > 0.05 or Recall@10 drops > 0.03 relative to baseline.

I've uploaded detailed CSVs to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-emb-evals (embeddings_benchmark_results.csv). Prompt templates attached.

Happy to sync Thu Mar 5 at 10:30am PT if that works.

Subject: Re: Embeddings technical notes and monitoring

Adding a few technical suggestions for ACME's evaluation plan:

- Similarity metric: use cosine for cross-language comparisons after mean-centering + L2-normalization; consider dot-product if using asymmetric rescoring with model logits.
- Dimensionality: 2048 helps capture fine-grained semantics but run SVD/PCA to quantify elbow for your dataset — we often see diminishing returns after ~1200 dims for product catalogs.
- Drift detection: two signals — distribution drift (KL on binned cosine) and task performance drift (Recall@k on a held-out query set).
- Embedding normalization: store normalized vectors to make thresholds portable across index configs.
- Indexing: HNSW with PQ on 2048 works well; set efConstruction/efSearch after a controlled latency sweep.

Operational notes:
- We'll provide a small evaluation harness (python notebook) that runs: vectorize -> index build -> recall/MRR calc -> drift report.
- Suggested watchlist: category-level recall breakdown for top 10 categories and language breakdown.

See Jira ticket for ops tracking: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/MLINF-342
